description: Hey, I'm Balwinder, a first year B.Tech IT student from Ludhiana. We're taking on the CLPS Lunar Mission Browser challenge, a simple web app to explore NASA's lunar missions without getting lost in the data. I'll handle the coding. Looking for 1-2 people good at UI/design or data visualization, or who just enjoy digging through NASA data. Fully online, 14-15 Nov. Hindi, English or Punjabi all fine. Beginners welcome, just stay active on chat 🙂
summary: Developed by Team Lunar Compile, the Lunar Landing Site Navigator is an agile, web-based mission-planning dashboard designed to optimize Lunar South Pole exploration. By synthesizing complex JPL Horizons ephemeris data into an interactive, chronological timeline, our application evaluates critical environmental constraints—such as solar power availability, direct-to-Earth communication windows, and geodetic slope limits. Unlike legacy tools that require manual parsing of fragmented tabular data, our Next.js-powered platform utilizes proprietary constraint-gating logic developed by Team Lunar Compile to instantly output composite "Go/No-Go" landing viability scores. This unified visual approach empowers mission engineers to rapidly evaluate backup landing dates during launch delays, bridges the communication gap between technical and scientific teams, and provides a zero-touch, browser-accessible interface for global public education. Built with React and TypeScript, it ensures a seamless, real-time mission control experience.
details:
Overview & Functionality by Team Lunar Compile:

The Lunar Landing Site Navigator is a web-based interactive tool engineered by Team Lunar Compile to translate complex lunar telemetry into an accessible, chronological visual dashboard. It dynamically filters potential South Pole landing sites based on strict safety and operational parameters, automatically mapping direct-to-Earth communication windows and solar power limits.

How It Works (Constraint-Gating Logic):

Instead of calculating Sun and Earth angles separately, Team Lunar Compile's proprietary algorithm unifies these metrics. It processes environmental constraints (such as timeToEarthsetHours, solar elevation, and power potential) to generate immediate landing viability scores and "Go/No-Go" statuses on a 30-day scrubbable timeline.

Impact & Benefits:

  1. Agile Rescheduling: Allows CLPS engineers to evaluate backup landing dates in seconds rather than hours during launch delays.
  2. Science Coordination: Provides a shared visual language bridging highly technical engineering telemetry with broader science teams.
  3. Accessibility: Zero-touch deployment means it is accessible instantly via any web browser, removing software installation barriers for both professionals and students.

Tech Stack & Tools: The platform is engineered using a modern, scalable web architecture by Team Lunar Compile. We utilized the Next.js (React) framework configured with TypeScript for robust type-safe logic, styled via Tailwind CSS for a responsive UI, and deployed globally via Vercel. Version control and CI/CD were managed through GitHub.

Creativity & Future Scope:

The novelty introduced by Team Lunar Compile lies in democratizing mission planning—moving away from raw tabular output to a unified chronological view. Our roadmap includes integrating 3D LOLA Topography mapping for true shadowing and multi-rover route optimization.
